title: Docs truth reconciliation: README status, benchmark-spec hash, sqlite driver decision record
description: Objective: close three measured doc-truth gaps (docs audit 2026-08-09). (1) README status paragraph understates the landed foundation: it names only test infra, evidence primitives and the graph kernel, while the repo also has a durable SQLite event store (pnpm verify:store), bounded-JSON input contracts, the control-room truth kernel and the fairness reference; rewrite the status paragraph to match reality at HEAD without claiming design freeze. (2) Benchmark-spec hash divergence: the design doc pins the benchmark spec at SHA-256 F8B84716... (Fable Revision 3) while docs/plans/2026-08-07-fable-fairness-aging-reference.md pins A62B9043...; determine which revision is current and record the resolution in a short docs/plans/ decision note. Do NOT edit the design doc (read-only, outside this repo); if the design-doc side is the stale one, escalate to the human instead. (3) node:sqlite driver: design section 4.1 requires a blocking packaging/fault spike before committing to a driver, but the store was built directly on Node 24 node:sqlite DatabaseSync with no recorded decision; write a retroactive decision record in docs/plans/ capturing the de-facto choice, the evidence in hand (store suite green, 357 tests) and the residual risk (release-candidate API), explicitly awaiting human ratification. NOT in scope: editing the external design doc, code changes. Owned paths: README.md and new files under docs/plans/ only. Verification: content review; pnpm test unaffected.
definitionOfDone: README status paragraph names the actually-landed foundation surfaces at HEAD
benchmark-spec hash divergence resolved in a decision note or explicitly escalated to the human
retroactive node:sqlite decision record exists in docs/plans/ marked as awaiting human ratification

Every surface the new status paragraph names exists on disk: `sqlite-event-store.ts`, `bounded-json.ts`, `control-room-model/src/index.ts`, `testkit/src/scheduler-fairness`, plus `test:store` and `verify:store` in package.json. They kept it attached to the graph-kernel bullet instead of promoting it, and gave every other surface its own scoped non-authority boundary. Rewriting the paragraph while letting that sentence float would have been the easy version and would have shipped a false claim in the same commit that fixed an understatement.

The note offers reconcile-the-pin versus ratify-in-the-manifest as a real open decision rather than implying a one-line hash bump — which is right, because Revision 4 deliberately dropped reciprocal pinning, so the design's fixed pin goes stale by construction on every future revision. DoD 3 — MET. `PROPOSED — AWAITING HUMAN RATIFICATION`, "Authority: none", design quoted verbatim rather than paraphrased, criteria scored one by one (1 met, 1 partial, 3 not met) instead of a narrative that would let a green suite read as a pass. I VERIFIED THE WORKER'S OWN FINDING 1 AT THE SOURCE, BECAUSE IT IS A PRODUCTION CLAIM AND IT HOLDS. They had written that the store *"refuses to open below a minimum SQLite version (`SQLITE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`)"*, then measured that the token is not an observable stable code and removed it. - `grep -rn SQLITE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED packages/store/src apps` returns **exactly one hit** — `sqlite-event-store.ts:173`, where it is a **message prefix on a plain `new Error(...)`**.
- It is **not** in the `DurableStoreErrorCode` union in `store-contracts.ts`.
- One hit total therefore also means **no test pins it**, so epic rail 6 is unexercised on that path, and the enclosing catch rewraps non-`DurableStoreError` throws as `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` — a caller cannot distinguish an unsupported SQLite build from a corrupt database.

So the README now says the store "refuses to open below a minimum SQLite version" — behaviourally true — **without** naming a code a caller cannot observe. That is the correct fix for a docs-scoped task: the underlying production gap is reported as a narrow follow-on (add the code to the union, throw typed, pin it with a test) and deliberately NOT fixed here, since this task owns docs only. Finding a defect in your own draft by measuring the sentence you just wrote is the behaviour this task was created to produce.
